old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of icicles hanging from the edge of a roof. The icicles are elongated and transparent, with a slight shimmer due to the light reflecting off their surfaces. They vary in size, with some appearing thicker at the base and tapering towards the tips. The icicles are attached to a dark-colored roof, which contrasts sharply with the bright, clear ice. In the background, there is a glimpse of snow on the roof's edge, indicating a cold environment. As the video progresses, small droplets of water can be seen falling from the icicles, suggesting that they are beginning to melt. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing solely on the icicles and their gradual transformation. The overall scene conveys a sense of winter's transition into spring, as the icicles slowly melt away.

caption: The video captures a close-up of several translucent icicles hanging from a beige gutter edge. A band of white snow runs along the top right, and a dark teal surface fills the left and lower background. The icicles themselves stay fixed, their banded glassy bodies catching the light without changing shape. The only visible motion is a continuous dripping cycle, as small droplets detach from the tips and fall through the dark area. Early in the excerpt a pair of droplets descends below the central icicles, then another slides down the left and one falls right. The dripping keeps an irregular rhythm, with droplets forming glossy bulges at the points and dropping through the middle of the frame. Tiny droplets vanish as they leave the lower edge, while a slight handheld drift shifts how much gutter shows at top. The process runs throughout, neither beginning nor ending in the visible window.

If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
